component.name: mediamanager
component.description: TAPPaaS module mediamanager: triage of its own critical/high CVEs (#788).

analysis.detail: Ubuntu's CUPS AppArmor profile. NixOS ships no such profile, and only cups' library is present (pulled in by gtk and qt); no cupsd runs.
RTSP client redirect loop in libavformat. On this VM ffmpeg/ffprobe only read local files under /data (Bazarr's subtitle extraction, Sonarr/Radarr's media analysis), never an rtsp:// URL.

memalign overflow in glibc 2.30-2.42 with an attacker-chosen alignment. The flagged glibc 2.44 (apps from nixos-unstable) is outside that range; the base's 2.42 is only called with fixed alignments by the services (.NET, nginx, Go).
strfmon/strfmon_l width-padding overflow. Nothing on the VM calls strfmon: .NET, Python, Node, Go and nginx format money themselves.
libssh is linked only by ffmpeg 9 as libavformat's SFTP client and no running process maps it; nothing on the VM opens an sftp:// URL (ffprobe reads local files).
Server-side GSSAPI key exchange. libssh is only ffmpeg's SFTP client here; the VM's sshd is OpenSSH.
TIFF decoding overflow. libtiff is loaded only by Bazarr through Pillow, and Bazarr never opens TIFF images (it handles subtitle text); gtk, gdk-pixbuf and openjpeg are not run by any service.
XSLT key() processing. libxslt is mapped by nginx (built-in xslt module, no xslt_stylesheet in the config) and by Bazarr through lxml (HTML parsing, no XSLT); nothing on the VM runs a stylesheet.
sshd GSSAPIAuthentication. This sshd is built without GSSAPI/Kerberos: not linked to libgssapi/libkrb5, and sshd -T lists no GSSAPI options.
sshd GSSAPI authentication state. This sshd is built without GSSAPI/Kerberos: not linked to libgssapi/libkrb5, and sshd -T lists no GSSAPI options.
Username injection in the ssh client's command line. No service on the VM starts ssh; only admins log in to it.
OpenSSL's own QUIC stack. Nothing on the VM speaks QUIC: nginx serves plain HTTP on 8080, the apps are TLS clients over TCP, oauth2-proxy uses Go's TLS.
Needs a TLS server that calls SSL_set_SSL_CTX mid-handshake. No TLS server runs on the VM: TLS ends at Caddy on the firewall, nginx serves plain HTTP.
DTLS retransmission. Nothing on the VM speaks DTLS: TLS over TCP as a client only, no TLS server.
NEW_CONNECTION_ID flood against OpenSSL's own QUIC stack. Nothing on the VM speaks QUIC: nginx serves plain HTTP, the apps are TLS clients over TCP.
